title: PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering): Measuring and Transferring a Member's Arrears at Enrollment
content:
PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) measures arrears across the member's portfolio, not only on the meter being enrolled.

**1. The arrears total.** The arrears to be transferred at enrollment are the positive account balance of the service account being enrolled plus the positive account balance of every final-billed service account of the same member, after any security deposit held on the enrolled service account has been applied to them; that is, the total of those positive balances less the deposit held on the enrolled service account. All of those balances are transferred; the member cannot leave one behind.

**2. Tier by band.** The tier is the one whose rate schedules and member types fit and whose band of transferred arrears, from its lowest through its highest figure inclusive, contains the arrears total.

**3. Band condition.** The arrears total must fall inside the band of the tier assigned at enrollment; when it exceeds the highest band available to the service account, the member must first pay the total down into a band. The total, and the balances and deposit it is built from, are read from the cooperative's records of the member's service accounts (their status and account balance) and of the deposit held on the enrolled service account, matched to the enrolling member.

**4. One transfer per source account.** Each source service account is transferred as its own arrears transfer for its whole positive balance, and each transfer is credited off that source account as a bill credit with the reason arrears transferred to PrePay Power.

**5. Retired clause.** The clause "A credit balance on the enrolled service account is carried in as a credit adjustment for a carried-in standard-billing credit and is never netted against another account's debt" is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for carrying a credit balance into an enrollment.

### Transferred-arrears bands

| Tier | Band (USD, inclusive) |
|---|---|
| PrePay Power Residential | 0.00 through 0.00 |
| PrePay Power Residential Recovery 25 | 0.01 through 500.00 |
| PrePay Power Residential Recovery 40 | 500.01 through 1500.00 |
| PrePay Power Seasonal | 0.00 through 250.00 |
| PrePay Power Outbuilding | 0.00 through 250.00 |
| PrePay Power Small Commercial | 0.00 through 0.00 |

### Worked illustrations (hypothetical balances, individual member on Schedule R)

- The enrolled account owes 180.00, one final-billed account of the member owes 420.00, and a deposit of 150.00 is held on the enrolled account. Arrears total: 180.00 plus 420.00, less 150.00, which is 450.00. It lies in 0.01 through 500.00, so the tier is PrePay Power Residential Recovery 25.
- The enrolled account owes 300.00 and two final-billed accounts owe 260.00 and 40.00, with no deposit. The total is 600.00, in the PrePay Power Residential Recovery 40 band, and three separate transfers are made: 300.00, 260.00 and 40.00, each credited off its own source account.
- The enrolled account owes 900.00 and a final-billed account owes 720.00, with no deposit: 1620.00 exceeds 1500.00, the top of the highest band available on Schedule R, so the member must first pay the total down into a band.

superseded_clauses: A credit balance on the enrolled service account is carried in as a prepay_credit_adjustment with adjustment_reason postpaid_credit_transfer and is never netted against another account's debt.
